answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may vote on a task or claim rewards. A participant who submits conflicting attestations loses the bond, while honest agents recover it after a review window. Creating a thousand sybils therefore requires locking a thousand bonds, not merely minting cheap accounts; the attacker pays capital costs and risks forfeiture. At a summit, sable might name the bond pool and nadir the minimum stake, but neither label changes the mechanism: it raises the price of influence rather than proving identities are unique.
